clues: It is one of only two publicly traded U.S. corporations to hold top AAA credit ratings from both Moody's and S&P Global Ratings.
It walked away from a preliminary letter of intent signed in March 2026 for a data center site in West Virginia.
It is targeting $170 billion in capital expenditures in 2026 to support its expanding artificial intelligence and cloud infrastructure.
It priced a ten-tranche, $25 billion bond deal that drew up to $115 billion in investor demand, its first such U.S. sale since 2017.
Unlike several hyperscaler rivals logging cash burns, it expects free cash flow to stay positive through its fiscal year ending June 2027.
Its Azure platform posted 48 percent revenue growth in fiscal first-quarter earnings reported in late October 2026.
